beats.intent: ThinkSR carries dense image features through encoding, windowing, repeated shared DQ-CTM thought ticks, and decoding.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process reads and updates it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. The window step partitions those features without dropping tokens. The DQ-CTM thought process repeats with shared parameters across ticks. The decoder converts the updated carrier back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through a compact recurrent thought stage
params.note: The loop returns to the thought stage itself.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines dense features from the low-resolution image, then windows that full feature field into tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier is the dense object that lets a compact thought process serve super-resolution. The encoder maps the low-resolution input into that field. The low-resolution image is the source signal. The dense feature field is kept persistent. The window partition turns that field into tokens while keeping every token.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before it is partitioned into windows

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; at 1.129M parameters it is second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129M parameters in Table 1’s ×4 lightweight super-resolution benchmark.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison shows that DQ-CTM-SR is not the cheapest model in this group. CATANet is the smallest at zero point five three five million parameters. RFDN is only slightly larger at zero point five five zero million. IMDN sits at zero point seven one five million. DQ-CTM-SR has one point one two nine million parameters, making it the second largest. CARN is largest at one point five nine two million.
